title: AbbVie vs. CVS Health: Which Healthcare Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Sara Appino
description: The article compares AbbVie and CVS Health as healthcare investment options in 2026. AbbVie, a biopharmaceutical company with a $438B market cap, is recommended as the better choice due to its focused growth trajectory, strong drug pipeline (Skyrizi and Rinvoq), and attractive dividend yield. CVS Health, a diversified healthcare provider with a $122B market cap managing 37 million medical members, is acknowledged as a turnaround story showing stabilization but is considered less compelling than AbbVie's growth prospects.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: AbbVie is recommended as the better buy with strong growth trajectory, accelerating drug portfolio (Skyrizi and Rinvoq growing at extraordinary pace), successful navigation of Humira biosimilar headwinds, emerging neuroscience portfolio, raised full-year outlook twice, and attractive dividend yield of 2.75%.

CVS Health is acknowledged as a genuine turnaround story with improving fundamentals (beat estimates, raised outlook twice, Aetna stabilization), but is considered less compelling than AbbVie. It trades at a conservative valuation (P/E 25.26) but faces headwinds from price compression, competition, and government policy exposure.

title: This Buffett Oil Stock Is Quietly Outperforming Chevron Under Greg Abel. Is It Worth Buying Now?
author: Thomas Niel
description: Occidental Petroleum has surged 36% since Greg Abel became Berkshire Hathaway's CEO in January, outperforming Chevron and the S&P 500. The rally was driven by U.S.-Iran tensions and crude oil price spikes. However, recent muted performance raises questions about sustainability. Future gains depend heavily on another crude oil price surge, particularly when China replenishes its strategic reserves, making Oxy a more volatile bet compared to Chevron's more stable outlook.

title: Worried About the Market? These Stocks Have a Track Record of Helping Investors Sleep at Night.
author: Brett Schafer
description: The article recommends three healthcare dividend growth stocks for investors seeking portfolio stability during market volatility: Johnson & Johnson (a Dividend King with 64 consecutive years of dividend increases), UnitedHealth Group (rebounding after recent challenges with a 2.26% yield), and McKesson (the largest U.S. pharmaceutical distributor with steady dividend growth). Healthcare is highlighted as a defensive sector due to non-discretionary spending patterns.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Recognized as a Dividend King with 64 consecutive years of dividend increases, 67% payout growth over 10 years, only one 25% drawdown in the last decade, and steady 6.6% year-over-year sales growth demonstrating reliable stability.

Despite recent 50% stock collapse due to temporary claims cost issues, the company has a strong long-term history with no drawdowns exceeding 25% post-2008, 271% dividend per share growth over 10 years, and positioned to benefit from rising healthcare spending with attractive 2.26% yield.

Described as a 'hidden winner' and sector leader in pharmaceutical distribution with 193% dividend per share growth over 10 years, relatively smooth 15-year performance aside from one 50% drawdown (2015-2018), and positioned to benefit from rising healthcare spending trends.

title: UnitedHealth Stock Has Rallied Big Since Berkshire Bailed. Did Warren Buffett and Greg Abel Blink Too Soon?
author: Brett Schafer
description: Berkshire Hathaway sold its UnitedHealth Group position in Q1 2026 at a loss after buying around $380/share in Q2 2025. The stock has since rebounded to $428, driven by improving profit margins as the company recovers from elevated medical loss ratios in 2025. UnitedHealth's medical care ratio is normalizing, and with strong secular tailwinds from healthcare inflation and potential earnings recovery to $25-30 billion, the stock appears undervalued at current levels.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock has rebounded significantly with improving profitability metrics. Medical loss ratio is normalizing from 88.9% to 86.7%, operating earnings are recovering, and the company benefits from secular healthcare inflation tailwinds. Forward earnings potential of $25-30 billion suggests attractive valuation at current $380B market cap with forward P/E of 15.
